cells.tense: You're here, and the door is open.
cells.verb: letting yourself be reached, before there's anything specific to feel about it
cells.place: in the strength that holds what has to be held
cells.ask: offer your attention to one thing today without deciding yet what it means — what comes back is a knowing that keeps deepening the longer you stay with it
cells.core: You can hold something heavy and still be open while you do it. Not armored, not collapsed — the capacity to bear is intact and the heart is still taking things in. That's rarer than either one alone. Nothing has been poured yet, and that's not a lack. It's the readiness itself.
cells.sheetLine: You're open and still holding. That's the whole thing working.

cells.tense: You're already braced for what's next.
cells.verb: having your heart open to everything at once, ahead of what's actually here
cells.place: in the strength that's carrying more than today asked it to
cells.ask: pick one thing you're doing and do it from clarity instead of pressure — what comes back is the ability to choose what's yours instead of being driven to take it all in
cells.core: You're feeling ahead of yourself. Before anything has arrived, you've already opened to it, prepared for it, made room for a load no one handed you. The receiving has turned into reaching, and the steadiness that holds you up is spending itself on what hasn't happened. Somewhere the bracing costs you the very thing you're bracing for.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying what hasn't arrived yet.

cells.tense: You stopped at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: keeping the heart closed when it could be taking something in
cells.place: in the strength that holds on by staying shut
cells.ask: let one moment be entirely new — no knowing what it is yet — and what comes back is the readiness you thought you'd lost
cells.core: You can bear the weight. What you're not doing is letting anything in while you carry it. Somewhere back there, opening to what was coming meant getting hurt, so the door got shut and stayed shut, and it worked — nothing gets through. The holding is doing all the work and none of it is being replenished. The strength is there. The receiving stopped.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding everything and letting nothing in.

cells.tense: The door is open and you're calling it nothing.
cells.verb: already receiving, already being moved, without calling it that
cells.place: in a strength that's borrowing from the openness and giving it no credit
cells.ask: name one thing you already know — the thing that landed without argument — and let it stand as yours
cells.core: Something in you is already being reached. People feel it, you feel it, it's shaping how you hold everything — and when you describe yourself it comes out as just being steady. The awareness is running. The claim on it isn't. You keep the door open and then say it was never open, and the keeping goes unnoticed by the one person it belongs to.
cells.sheetLine: You're already taking it in. You call it just holding on.
